design_parameters.raw: - Differential pairs:      4 per bidirectional link (8 wires)
- Data signalling rate:    2 Mbps to 200+ Mbps (default 10 Mbit/s at reset)
- Data character:          10 bits (parity + data-control flag + 8 data bits)
- Control character:       4 bits (parity + data-control flag + 2 control bits)

signaling_summary: Each SpaceWire link direction carries a Data (D) signal and a Strobe (S) signal, each a low-voltage differential signalling (LVDS) pair (D+/D-, S+/S-). Data-Strobe (DS) encoding ensures exactly one of the two signals changes per bit, so the receiver recovers the clock as Clock = Data XOR Strobe. There is no separately forwarded clock wire. A bidirectional link uses four LVDS pairs (eight wires).
modulation: LVDS differential on Data (D+/D-) and Strobe (S+/S-) per direction.
clocking: Embedded clock recovered by Data-Strobe decoding: Clock = Data XOR Strobe. Because only one of D/S changes per bit, the link tolerates large skew between the Data and Strobe wires (up to almost one bit period).

transmitter_specs_canonical.encoding: Data-Strobe (DS); Strobe toggles when Data does not

receiver_specs_canonical.skew_tolerance: tolerates up to almost one bit period of D/S skew

encoding_role_in_analog: Data-Strobe encoding over LVDS is the heart of the SpaceWire signal level: the Strobe signal changes whenever Data does not, so the clock is the exclusive-OR of Data and Strobe. This avoids a forwarded clock and tolerates large wire-to-wire skew; integrity at the character level comes from odd parity, and at the link level from disconnect / escape / credit error detection.
